spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m7p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Robots == {"r1", "r2", "r3"}
none == "none"

VARIABLES slot, active, retired, cap, casFails
vars == << slot, active, retired, cap, casFails >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ slot \in Robots \cup {none}
    /\ active \subseteq Robots
    /\ retired \subseteq Robots
    /\ cap \in 0..3
    /\ casFails \in 0..6

Init ==
    /\ slot = none
    /\ active = Robots
    /\ retired = {}
    /\ cap = 3
    /\ casFails = 0

Claim(r) ==
    /\ r \in active
    /\ slot = none
    /\ Cardinality(active) <= cap
    /\ slot' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED << active, retired, cap, casFails >>

FailClaim(r) ==
    /\ r \in active
    /\ slot # none
    /\ slot # r
    /\ casFails < 6
    /\ casFails' = casFails + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << slot, active, retired, cap >>

Retire(r) ==
    /\ slot = r
    /\ r \in active
    /\ active' = active \ {r}
    /\ retired' = retired \cup {r}
    /\ slot' = none
    /\ UNCHANGED << cap, casFails >>

RaiseCap ==
    /\ cap < 3
    /\ cap' = cap + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << slot, active, retired, casFails >>

LowerCap ==
    /\ cap > 0
    /\ cap' = cap - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << slot, active, retired, casFails >>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Claim(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : FailClaim(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Retire(r)
    \/ RaiseCap
    \/ LowerCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RetiredNeverActive == active \cap retired = {}
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RetiredNeverActive
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet coordinates the permanent decommissioning of individual
robots. A single compare-and-swap register (the "retire slot") is used to grant
one robot at a time the exclusive right to shut itself down. Each robot is
initially active. To retire, a robot must first CAS the retire slot from empty
to its own id; if the slot is already claimed by another robot the CAS fails and
a failure counter is bumped. Only the robot that currently holds the slot may
perform the irreversible retire action, which moves it out of the active set and
into the retired set and releases the slot back to empty. Retirement is
permanent: nothing ever moves a robot back into the active set. The fleet's
capacity can change at runtime -- an operator may raise or lower the cap -- and a
robot may only claim the retire slot while the number of active robots is within
the current capacity. Actions: CAS-claim the slot, a failed CAS attempt, the
irreversible retire, raise capacity, lower capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No robot is ever simultaneously active and retired, so the
irreversible retire action takes effect at most once per robot.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m2p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Locks == {"l1", "l2", "l3", "l4"}
MaxPaired == 2
none == "none"

VARIABLES proposed, votes, paired, beat
vars == << proposed, votes, paired, beat >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ proposed \in Locks \cup {none}
    /\ votes \subseteq Locks
    /\ paired \subseteq Locks
    /\ beat \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ proposed = none
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ paired = {}
    /\ beat = 0

Propose(l) ==
    /\ proposed = none
    /\ l \notin paired
    /\ proposed' = l
    /\ UNCHANGED << votes, paired, beat >>

CastVote(l) ==
    /\ l \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED << proposed, paired, beat >>

Commit(l) ==
    /\ proposed = l
    /\ l \in votes
    /\ Cardinality(paired) < MaxPaired
    /\ paired' = paired \cup {l}
    /\ votes' = votes \ {l}
    /\ proposed' = none
    /\ UNCHANGED beat

Abort(l) ==
    /\ proposed = l
    /\ proposed' = none
    /\ UNCHANGED << votes, paired, beat >>

Unpair(l) ==
    /\ l \in paired
    /\ paired' = paired \ {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED << proposed, votes, beat >>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beat' = (beat + 1) % 3
    /\ UNCHANGED << proposed, votes, paired >>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Propose(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : CastVote(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Commit(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Abort(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Unpair(l)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinCapacity == Cardinality(paired) <= MaxPaired
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinCapacity
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network onboards new locks through a two-phase-commit
protocol run by a hub. There is a hard ceiling MaxPaired on how many locks may be
simultaneously paired to the hub. To onboard a lock the hub first proposes it,
then a participant emits a yes-vote message into the network. The network is
asynchronous and messages can be reordered: votes sit in an unordered in-flight
set and may be delivered in any order relative to when they were sent. The hub
commits an onboarding only when a yes-vote for the currently proposed lock is
present AND the paired set still has room under MaxPaired; committing moves the
lock into the paired set and consumes its vote. The hub may abort the current
proposal, and a paired lock may later be unpaired to free a slot. Actions:
propose a lock, emit a (reorderable) yes-vote, commit the onboarding, abort the
proposal, unpair a lock, tick the heartbeat.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of locks paired to the hub never exceeds the fixed
capacity MaxPaired.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m6p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Inst == {"A", "B"}
LeaseLen == 2
MaxClock == 3
none == "none"

VARIABLES owner, expiry, clock, st, pool
vars == << owner, expiry, clock, st, pool >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Inst \cup {none}
    /\ expiry \in 0..(MaxClock + LeaseLen)
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ st \in [Inst -> {"idle", "critical"}]
    /\ pool \in 0..3

NoneCritical == \A j \in Inst : st[j] = "idle"

Init ==
    /\ owner = none
    /\ expiry = 0
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ st = [i \in Inst |-> "idle"]
    /\ pool = 3

Acquire(i) ==
    /\ NoneCritical
    /\ (owner = none \/ expiry <= clock)
    /\ owner' = i
    /\ expiry' = clock + LeaseLen
    /\ UNCHANGED << clock, st, pool >>

Enter(i) ==
    /\ owner = i
    /\ expiry > clock
    /\ st[i] = "idle"
    /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![i] = "critical"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, expiry, clock, pool >>

Exit(i) ==
    /\ st[i] = "critical"
    /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ owner' = none
    /\ pool' = (pool + 1) % 4
    /\ UNCHANGED << expiry, clock >>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, expiry, st, pool >>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Acquire(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Enter(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Exit(i)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CriticalIsOwner == \A i \in Inst : st[i] = "critical" => owner = i
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CriticalIsOwner
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker is accessed by two independent server instances,
A and B, that share one physical inventory pool. Exclusive write access to the
pool is granted through a lease that carries an expiry deadline. A logical clock
advances over time. An instance may acquire the lease only when no instance is
currently inside its critical section and the outstanding lease is empty or has
already expired against the clock, stamping the lease with itself as owner and a
fresh expiry. An instance may enter its critical section -- where it mutates the
shared pool -- only while it holds the lease and the lease has not expired. On
exit it releases the lease and updates the pool. The clock ticks forward, which
can silently expire a lease that has not yet been entered. Actions: acquire the
lease, enter the critical section, exit the critical section, tick the clock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: An instance is in its critical section only while it is the
recorded lease owner, so the two instances never both hold write access to the
shared inventory pool at once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m3p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Drones == {"d1", "d2", "d3"}
MaxTerm == 3
MaxPool == 2

VARIABLES leader, curTerm, term, mode, pool
vars == << leader, curTerm, term, mode, pool >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Drones
    /\ curTerm \in 1..MaxTerm
    /\ term \in [Drones -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ mode \in [Drones -> {"standby", "commanding"}]
    /\ pool \in 0..MaxPool

Init ==
    /\ leader = "d1"
    /\ curTerm = 1
    /\ term = [d \in Drones |-> IF d = "d1" THEN 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ mode = [d \in Drones |-> "standby"]
    /\ pool = MaxPool

Failover(d) ==
    /\ curTerm < MaxTerm
    /\ d # leader
    /\ mode[leader] = "standby"
    /\ leader' = d
    /\ curTerm' = curTerm + 1
    /\ term' = [term EXCEPT ![d] = curTerm + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << mode, pool >>

Command(d) ==
    /\ leader = d
    /\ term[d] = curTerm
    /\ mode[d] = "standby"
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "commanding"]
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, curTerm, term >>

Release(d) ==
    /\ mode[d] = "commanding"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "standby"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, curTerm, term, pool >>

Refill ==
    /\ pool < MaxPool
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, curTerm, term, mode >>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Failover(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Command(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Release(d)
    \/ Refill

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CommandAuthorized ==
    \A d \in Drones : mode[d] = "commanding" => (leader = d /\ term[d] = curTerm)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CommandAuthorized
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm is split into two independent squads that
share one sensor pool. Within the swarm a single leader is elected to command the
shared pool, and leadership can fail over: the current leader may crash and, in
the same failover step, a new leader is installed under a strictly higher term
number. Each drone records the term under which it last became leader. A drone
may command the shared pool only while it is the registered leader and its
recorded term equals the current term; a stale ex-leader whose term is behind
must not command. Commanding draws one unit from the shared pool; releasing
returns the drone to standby, and the pool can be refilled. Actions: fail over to
a new leader, command the pool, release command, refill the pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A drone commands the shared sensor pool only when it is the
current-term registered leader, so at most one drone across both squads ever
commands the pool at a time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m2p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

MaxCap == 5

VARIABLES available, reserved, enrolled, capacity
vars == << available, reserved, enrolled, capacity >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ available \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ reserved \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ enrolled \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ available = 3
    /\ reserved = 0
    /\ enrolled = 0
    /\ capacity = 3

Prepare ==
    /\ available > 0
    /\ available' = available - 1
    /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << enrolled, capacity >>

Commit ==
    /\ reserved > 0
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << available, capacity >>

Abort ==
    /\ reserved > 0
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ available' = available + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << enrolled, capacity >>

Drop ==
    /\ enrolled > 0
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled - 1
    /\ available' = available + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << reserved, capacity >>

AddSeat ==
    /\ capacity < MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ available' = available + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << reserved, enrolled >>

RemoveSeat ==
    /\ available > 0
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ available' = available - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << reserved, enrolled >>

Next ==
    \/ Prepare
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Drop
    \/ AddSeat
    \/ RemoveSeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SeatsConserved == available + reserved + enrolled = capacity
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SeatsConserved
nl:
A university course-registration system manages the seats of a single popular
course through a two-phase-commit protocol. Every seat is always in exactly one
of three buckets: available, reserved (held mid-transaction), or enrolled. To
register, the coordinator first moves a seat from available to reserved (the
prepare phase); it then either commits, moving that seat from reserved to
enrolled, or aborts, moving it back from reserved to available. An enrolled
student may later drop, returning that seat from enrolled to available. The
course capacity can change at runtime: an administrator may add a seat (raising
capacity and the available pool together) or remove a currently-available seat
(lowering both together). No seat is ever created or destroyed except through
these capacity adjustments, which move the total in lockstep. Actions: prepare a
reservation, commit an enrollment, abort a reservation, drop an enrollment, add a
seat, remove a seat.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of available, reserved, and enrolled seats always
sums exactly to the current course capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m9p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Books == {"b1", "b2", "b3"}
MaxHold == 2
MaxEpoch == 3

VARIABLES epoch, requests, shelf, beat
vars == << epoch, requests, shelf, beat >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
    /\ requests \subseteq (Books \X (1..MaxEpoch))
    /\ shelf \subseteq Books
    /\ beat \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 1
    /\ requests = {}
    /\ shelf = {}
    /\ beat = 0

Issue(b) ==
    /\ << b, epoch >> \notin requests
    /\ b \notin shelf
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {<< b, epoch >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, shelf, beat >>

Grant(b) ==
    /\ << b, epoch >> \in requests
    /\ b \notin shelf
    /\ Cardinality(shelf) < MaxHold
    /\ shelf' = shelf \cup {b}
    /\ requests' = requests \ {<< b, epoch >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, beat >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << requests, shelf, beat >>

Release(b) ==
    /\ b \in shelf
    /\ shelf' = shelf \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, requests, beat >>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beat' = (beat + 1) % 3
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, requests, shelf >>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Books : Issue(b)
    \/ \E b \in Books : Grant(b)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E b \in Books : Release(b)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ShelfWithinCapacity == Cardinality(shelf) <= MaxHold
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ShelfWithinCapacity
nl:
A library book-reservation system holds at most MaxHold books on the reserve
shelf at once. Reservation requests arrive over an asynchronous channel and can
be reordered: pending requests sit in an unordered set, each tagged with the
configuration epoch under which it was issued. Periodically the system undergoes
an epoch-numbered reconfiguration that bumps the current epoch; requests issued
under an older epoch are stale and are discarded rather than granted. A request
is granted -- placing its book on the reserve shelf -- only if it carries the
current epoch and the shelf still has room under MaxHold. Books are later
released from the shelf, and a background heartbeat advances periodically. Actions: issue a (reorderable, epoch-tagged) request,
grant a current-epoch request, reconfigure to a new epoch, release a held book, tick the heartbeat.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of books on the reserve shelf never exceeds the fixed
hold capacity MaxHold.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m2p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Robots == {"r1", "r2"}
Slots == {"s1", "s2"}
none == "none"
noPair == << "none", "none" >>

VARIABLES owner, free, prepared, overrides
vars == << owner, free, prepared, overrides >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Robots \cup {none}]
    /\ free \subseteq Slots
    /\ prepared \in (Robots \X Slots) \cup {noPair}
    /\ overrides \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> none]
    /\ free = Slots
    /\ prepared = noPair
    /\ overrides = 0

Prepare(r, s) ==
    /\ prepared = noPair
    /\ s \in free
    /\ prepared' = << r, s >>
    /\ UNCHANGED << owner, free, overrides >>

Commit ==
    /\ prepared # noPair
    /\ prepared[2] \in free
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![prepared[2]] = prepared[1]]
    /\ free' = free \ {prepared[2]}
    /\ prepared' = noPair
    /\ UNCHANGED overrides

Release(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] # none
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = none]
    /\ free' = free \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED << prepared, overrides >>

Override(r, s) ==
    /\ overrides < 2
    /\ owner[s] # none
    /\ owner[s] # r
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << free, prepared >>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, s \in Slots : Prepare(r, s)
    \/ Commit
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, s \in Slots : Override(r, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FreeIffUnowned == \A s \in Slots : (s \in free) <=> (owner[s] = none)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FreeIffUnowned
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet assigns robots to charging-dock slots through a
two-phase-commit handshake. Each slot is either free or owns exactly one robot;
the set of free slots and the per-slot owner map are kept as two views of the
same allocation. To assign a robot the coordinator first prepares a (robot, slot)
pair naming a currently free slot; committing that pair records the robot as the
slot's owner and removes the slot from the free set at the same time. Releasing a
slot clears its owner and returns it to the free set. A privileged admin override
can forcibly reassign an already-occupied slot to a different robot without going
through the prepare phase, but it must leave the slot occupied (never marking it
free while owned). Actions: prepare an assignment, commit the prepared
assignment, release a slot, admin-override a slot's owner.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A slot is in the free set if and only if it has no owner, so no
slot is ever allocated to a robot while still advertised as free (which would
allow a second robot to be allocated the same slot).

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m4p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Inst == {"A", "B"}
MaxQ == 3
none == "none"

VARIABLES holder, st, queue, beat
vars == << holder, st, queue, beat >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Inst \cup {none}
    /\ st \in [Inst -> {"idle", "printing"}]
    /\ queue \in 0..MaxQ
    /\ beat \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ holder = none
    /\ st = [i \in Inst |-> "idle"]
    /\ queue = 0
    /\ beat = 0

Enqueue ==
    /\ queue < MaxQ
    /\ queue' = queue + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, st, beat >>

Acquire(i) ==
    /\ holder = none
    /\ st[i] = "idle"
    /\ holder' = i
    /\ UNCHANGED << st, queue, beat >>

Start(i) ==
    /\ holder = i
    /\ st[i] = "idle"
    /\ queue > 0
    /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![i] = "printing"]
    /\ queue' = queue - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, beat >>

Finish(i) ==
    /\ st[i] = "printing"
    /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ holder' = none
    /\ UNCHANGED << queue, beat >>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beat' = (beat + 1) % 3
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, st, queue >>

Next ==
    \/ Enqueue
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Acquire(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Start(i)
    \/ \E i \in Inst : Finish(i)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PrintingHoldsToken == \A i \in Inst : st[i] = "printing" => holder = i
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PrintingHoldsToken
nl:
A print-shop job spooler serves two independent client instances that share one
physical printer. Jobs wait in a single bounded work queue: enqueueing is subject
to backpressure and is refused once the queue reaches its maximum depth. Access
to the shared printer is guarded by a mutex token; an instance must acquire the
token before it can start printing, and only the token holder may be in the
printing state. Starting to print consumes one queued job; finishing releases the
token back. A background heartbeat advances periodically. Actions: enqueue a job (respecting backpressure), acquire the printer
token, start printing a queued job, finish printing and release the token, tick the heartbeat.
SAFETY PROPERTY: An instance is in the printing state only while it holds the
printer token, so the two instances never print on the shared printer at the same
time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m8p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Parts == {"p1", "p2"}
Rooms == {"o1", "o2"}
none == "none"

VARIABLES coarse, fine, booker, reqs
vars == << coarse, fine, booker, reqs >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Parts \cup {none}
    /\ fine \in [Rooms -> Parts \cup {none}]
    /\ booker \in [Rooms -> Parts \cup {none}]
    /\ reqs \subseteq Parts

Init ==
    /\ coarse = none
    /\ fine = [rm \in Rooms |-> none]
    /\ booker = [rm \in Rooms |-> none]
    /\ reqs = {}

RequestCoarse(p) ==
    /\ p \notin reqs
    /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, booker >>

GrantCoarse(p) ==
    /\ coarse = none
    /\ p \in reqs
    /\ coarse' = p
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED << fine, booker >>

GrantFine(p, rm) ==
    /\ coarse = p
    /\ fine[rm] = none
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![rm] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, booker, reqs >>

Book(p, rm) ==
    /\ fine[rm] = p
    /\ booker[rm] = none
    /\ booker' = [booker EXCEPT ![rm] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarse, fine, reqs >>

Release(p) ==
    /\ coarse = p
    /\ coarse' = none
    /\ fine' = [rm \in Rooms |-> IF fine[rm] = p THEN none ELSE fine[rm]]
    /\ booker' = [rm \in Rooms |-> IF booker[rm] = p THEN none ELSE booker[rm]]
    /\ UNCHANGED reqs

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Parts : RequestCoarse(p)
    \/ \E p \in Parts : GrantCoarse(p)
    \/ \E p \in Parts, rm \in Rooms : GrantFine(p, rm)
    \/ \E p \in Parts, rm \in Rooms : Book(p, rm)
    \/ \E p \in Parts : Release(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BookingAuthorized ==
    \A rm \in Rooms :
        booker[rm] # none => (coarse = booker[rm] /\ fine[rm] = booker[rm])
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BookingAuthorized
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler protects its rooms with hierarchical locks: a
coarse lock on the surgical wing must be held before any fine lock on an
individual room can be granted, and a room may be booked only by the participant
holding that room's fine lock. Coarse-lock requests arrive over an asynchronous
channel and can be reordered: they wait in an unordered set and may be granted in
any order. The wing's coarse lock is held by at most one participant at a time.
When a participant releases, it gives up the coarse lock and, in the same step,
all fine locks and bookings it held become void -- a stale ex-holder retains
nothing. Actions: request the coarse lock (reorderable), grant the coarse lock to
a waiting requester, grant a room's fine lock to the coarse-lock holder, book a
room, release everything held.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A room shows a booking only for a participant that currently
holds both the surgical wing's coarse lock and that room's fine lock, so no stale
or unauthorized participant ever retains a booking.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m1p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Nodes == 0..2
Books == {"b1", "b2", "b3"}
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES token, circulating, archived, capacity
vars == << token, circulating, archived, capacity >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Nodes
    /\ circulating \subseteq Books
    /\ archived \subseteq Books
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ circulating = Books
    /\ archived = {}
    /\ capacity = 2

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % 3
    /\ UNCHANGED << circulating, archived, capacity >>

Archive(b) ==
    /\ b \in circulating
    /\ Cardinality(archived) < capacity
    /\ circulating' = circulating \ {b}
    /\ archived' = archived \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, capacity >>

RaiseCap ==
    /\ capacity < MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, circulating, archived >>

LowerCap ==
    /\ capacity > Cardinality(archived)
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, circulating, archived >>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E b \in Books : Archive(b)
    \/ RaiseCap
    \/ LowerCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NeverBothStates == circulating \cap archived = {}
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NeverBothStates
nl:
A library book-reservation system runs a maintenance token ring over its shelving
nodes. Exactly one node holds the maintenance token at any time, and the token is
passed around the ring. Only the node currently holding the token may perform the
irreversible archival of a book: archival permanently removes the book from the
circulating collection and files it in the archive, and nothing ever returns an
archived book to circulation. The archive has a capacity that changes at runtime

circulating book (token holder only), raise the archive capacity, lower the
archive capacity.

irreversible archival of any given book takes effect at most once.

---- MODULE W4Od2m6p0t3 ----

granted by a lease that carries an expiry deadline measured against a logical
clock. A robot may take the lease only when the bay is empty and no valid lease
is outstanding (none held, or the current one expired), stamping itself as holder
with a fresh expiry. Only a robot holding an unexpired lease may enter the bay. A
robot in the bay may be slow but never fails: it can stall, letting the clock
advance while it keeps the bay, and it eventually exits, releasing the lease.

exit the bay, tick the clock.

holder, so at most one robot -- the lease holder -- is ever in the bay at once.

token ring; exactly one node holds the dispatch token at a time and passes it
around the ring. Print requests arrive asynchronously and can be reordered: they
wait in an unordered set and may be picked up in any order. Only the node
currently holding the dispatch token may begin servicing a request, and a node
counts as actively servicing only while it holds the token. The token is passed
on only when the current holder is not mid-service, so a stale node that has given
up the token is never left servicing. A background heartbeat advances periodically. Actions: pass the dispatch token to the
next node, submit a (reorderable) print request, start servicing a request (token
holder only), finish servicing, tick the heartbeat.

the dispatch token, so no stale non-holder node ever services work.

    /\ pending' = pending + 1

    /\ pending' = pending - 1

    /\ depot' = depot + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << rc, budget >>

    /\ depot' = depot + 1

NEXT Next

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares a central battery depot. Charge units move between
the depot and two robots via a two-phase-commit transfer. To hand charge to a
robot the depot first prepares a unit -- moving it from the depot store into an
in-flight pending buffer -- then either commits it into that robot's onboard
charge or aborts it back to the depot. A robot may also return a unit of its
onboard charge to the depot. The fleet's total charge budget changes at runtime:
an operator can add a unit to the budget (and the depot) or reclaim a unit from
the depot, moving the budget in lockstep. Charge is never otherwise created or
destroyed. Actions: prepare a transfer, commit a transfer to a robot, abort a
transfer, return a robot's charge, add a budget unit, reclaim a budget unit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The depot store, the in-flight pending buffer, and the two
robots' onboard charge always sum exactly to the current total charge budget.

---- MODULE W4Od8m9p1t4 ----

    /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
    /\ pending \subseteq (Updates \X (1..MaxEpoch))
    /\ applied \subseteq Updates
    /\ acked \subseteq Updates
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

    /\ epoch = 1
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ capacity = 2

    /\ << u, epoch >> \notin pending
    /\ Cardinality(pending) < capacity
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {<< u, epoch >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, applied, acked, capacity >>

Apply(u) ==
    /\ << u, epoch >> \in pending
    /\ u \notin applied
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {u}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {<< u, epoch >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, acked, capacity >>

Acknowledge(u) ==
    /\ u \in applied
    /\ u \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, pending, applied, capacity >>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << pending, applied, acked, capacity >>

RaiseCap ==
    /\ capacity < MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, pending, applied, acked >>

LowerCap ==
    /\ capacity > 1
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, pending, applied, acked >>

    \/ \E u \in Updates : Submit(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updates : Apply(u)
    \/ \E u \in Updates : Acknowledge(u)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ RaiseCap

nl:

absorbs a stream of updates. Updates are submitted into a bounded pending buffer
whose capacity changes at runtime as the registrar raises or lowers it; each
submission is tagged with the configuration epoch in force. An epoch-numbered
reconfiguration bumps the current epoch, and only a pending update carrying the
current epoch is ever applied to the record. An update is acknowledged to its
submitter only after it has actually been applied. Actions: submit an update
(bounded by pending capacity), apply a current-epoch pending update to the
record, acknowledge an already-applied update, reconfigure to a new epoch, raise
the pending capacity, lower the pending capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every acknowledged update has been applied to the enrollment
record, so no acknowledged update is ever lost.

two-phase-commit protocol; a finalized grade is irreversible and permanent. To
finalize, a student's record is first prepared, then committed to the finalized
set. A participating node can crash silently at any point while a record is
prepared: the prepare is silently dropped and the record is set aside as crashed,
from which it may later recover back to the open pool. A background monitor
emits a periodic heartbeat. A record can be prepared only when it is not already
finalized, so finalization cannot be re-run on an already-finalized grade.

silently, recover a crashed record, tick the monitor heartbeat.

irreversible finalization of any grade takes effect at most once.

using a compare-and-swap register as a generation counter. A token is always
either in the free pool or granted to a student; the two counts always account
for every token. A grant performs a successful compare-and-swap -- bumping the

revoke a granted token, register a failed stale compare-and-swap, admin-override
a grant.

always exactly the fixed token total, so no token is created or destroyed.

two-phase-commit protocol into a durable log. Each committed update is stamped
with the next sequence number, so the log of applied sequence numbers is meant to
be a gap-free prefix. To commit, the coordinator prepares the next sequence
number, then either commits it -- appending that number to the applied log and
advancing the version -- or aborts, discarding the prepared number without
advancing. A trackside participant may be slow but never fails: a delay tick lets
time pass without progress. Actions: prepare the next sequence number, commit the
prepared update, abort the prepared update, tick a delay.

contiguous range from 1 to the current version, so no committed update leaves a
gap in the log.

    /\ o \in queue

    /\ slotOf[o] = none
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = o]
    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![o] = s]
    /\ queue' = queue \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED beat

    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![o] = none]

completed order's slot, crash an order silently.

same order back, so no slot is ever double-allocated to two different orders.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every runway slot that currently holds an aircraft assignment has
that assignment durably logged, so no committed assignment is ever lost.

    /\ sold = {}
    /\ intents = {}
    /\ retries = 0
    /\ beat = 0

Stage(i) ==
    /\ i \in available
    /\ << i, version >> \notin intents
    /\ intents' = intents \cup {<< i, version >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, available, sold, retries, beat >>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ << i, version >> \in intents
    /\ i \in available
    /\ available' = available \ {i}
    /\ sold' = sold \cup {i}
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ intents' = intents \ {<< i, version >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << retries, beat >>

Conflict(i, v) ==
    /\ << i, v >> \in intents
    /\ v # version
    /\ retries < 3
    /\ intents' = intents \ {<< i, v >>}
    /\ retries' = retries + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, available, sold, beat >>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beat' = (beat + 1) % 3
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, available, sold, intents, retries >>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Items : Stage(i)
    \/ \E i \in Items : Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Items, v \in 0..3 : Conflict(i, v)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NeverAvailableAndSold == available \cap sold = {}
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NeverAvailableAndSold
nl:
A vending-machine network finalizes drink sales using optimistic locking over a
shared inventory version. Each item is either available or sold; a sale is
irreversible and a sold item never returns to available. A buyer first stages a
purchase intent, recording the inventory version it observed; staged intents
arrive asynchronously and can be reordered in an unordered set. A commit succeeds
only if the observed version still matches the current version, in which case the
item moves from available to sold and the version is bumped. If the observed
version is stale the intent conflicts and is dropped, and a retry tally is bumped.
A heartbeat advances periodically. Actions: stage a purchase intent (reorderable),
commit a matching intent, drop a conflicting stale intent, tick the heartbeat.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No item is ever both available and sold, so the irreversible sale
of any item takes effect at most once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m5p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Bags == {"g1", "g2"}
Controllers == {"c1", "c2", "c3"}
Gates == {"A", "B"}
Quorum == 2
none == "none"

VARIABLES routed, acked, votes, admins
vars == << routed, acked, votes, admins >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ routed \in [Bags -> Gates \cup {none}]
    /\ acked \subseteq Bags
    /\ votes \in [Bags -> SUBSET Controllers]
    /\ admins \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ routed = [b \in Bags |-> none]
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ votes = [b \in Bags |-> {}]
    /\ admins = 0

Vote(b, c) ==
    /\ c \notin votes[b]
    /\ routed[b] = none
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = votes[b] \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED << routed, acked, admins >>

Commit(b, g) ==
    /\ routed[b] = none
    /\ Cardinality(votes[b]) >= Quorum
    /\ routed' = [routed EXCEPT ![b] = g]
    /\ UNCHANGED << acked, votes, admins >>

Acknowledge(b) ==
    /\ routed[b] # none
    /\ b \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED << routed, votes, admins >>

AdminRoute(b, g) ==
    /\ admins < 2
    /\ routed[b] = none
    /\ routed' = [routed EXCEPT ![b] = g]
    /\ admins' = admins + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED << acked, votes >>

Clear(b) ==
    /\ routed[b] # none
    /\ routed' = [routed EXCEPT ![b] = none]
    /\ acked' = acked \ {b}
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED admins

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bags, c \in Controllers : Vote(b, c)
    \/ \E b \in Bags, g \in Gates : Commit(b, g)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Acknowledge(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bags, g \in Gates : AdminRoute(b, g)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : Clear(b)

AckedIsRouted == \A b \in Bags : b \in acked => routed[b] # none
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AckedIsRouted
nl:
An airport baggage router commits routing decisions by quorum vote. A bag's route
becomes durable only after a quorum of the routing controllers have voted for it,
at which point the bag is marked routed to a gate. A routing is acknowledged to
the check-in desk only after the bag has actually been routed. A privileged admin
override can route a bag directly, bypassing the quorum. A routed bag may later be
cleared, which withdraws its acknowledgement and resets its votes so it can be
re-routed. Actions: cast a controller vote for a bag, commit a bag's route once it
has quorum, acknowledge a routed bag, admin-override a bag's route, clear a routed
bag.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every acknowledged bag currently has a durable route to a gate,
so no acknowledged routing decision is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od11m3p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Nodes == {"n1", "n2"}
Jobs == {"j1", "j2", "j3"}
MaxTerm == 2
none == "none"

VARIABLES leader, term, pending, archived, beat
vars == << leader, term, pending, archived, beat >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {none}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ pending \subseteq Jobs
    /\ archived \subseteq Jobs
    /\ beat \in 0..2

Init ==
    /\ leader = none
    /\ term = 0
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ archived = {}
    /\ beat = 0

Elect(n) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED << pending, archived, beat >>

Request(j) ==
    /\ j \notin pending
    /\ j \notin archived
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, term, archived, beat >>

Archive(j) ==
    /\ leader # none
    /\ j \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {j}
    /\ archived' = archived \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, term, beat >>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beat' = (beat + 1) % 3
    /\ UNCHANGED << leader, term, pending, archived >>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Request(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Archive(j)
    \/ Heartbeat

PendingNotArchived == pending \cap archived = {}
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PendingNotArchived
nl:
A print-shop job spooler permanently archives completed jobs; archival is
irreversible and an archived job is never un-archived. Archival requests arrive
asynchronously and can be reordered: they wait in an unordered pending set. The
spooler elects a leader node under increasing term numbers, and only the current
leader may move a pending job into the archive. A background heartbeat advances
periodically. A job cannot be re-requested for archival once it is archived.
Actions: elect a leader under a new term, request archival of a job (reorderable),
archive a pending job (leader only), tick the heartbeat.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No job is ever both pending archival and already archived, so the
irreversible archival of any job takes effect at most once.

---- MODULE W4Od16m1p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

Stations == 0..2
Rx == {"x1", "x2", "x3"}
Cap == 2

VARIABLES token, pool, tray, crashed
vars == << token, pool, tray, crashed >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Stations
    /\ pool \subseteq Rx
    /\ tray \subseteq Rx
    /\ crashed \subseteq Stations

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ tray = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (token + 1) % 3
    /\ UNCHANGED << pool, tray, crashed >>

Submit(r) ==
    /\ r \notin pool
    /\ r \notin tray
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, tray, crashed >>

Load(r) ==
    /\ r \in pool
    /\ Cardinality(tray) < Cap
    /\ tray' = tray \cup {r}
    /\ pool' = pool \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, crashed >>

Dispense(r) ==
    /\ r \in tray
    /\ tray' = tray \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, pool, crashed >>

Crash(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, pool, tray >>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E r \in Rx : Submit(r)
    \/ \E r \in Rx : Load(r)
    \/ \E r \in Rx : Dispense(r)
    \/ \E n \in Stations : Crash(n)

TrayWithinCap == Cardinality(tray) <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TrayWithinCap
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser loads filled prescriptions onto a dispensing
tray that holds at most Cap items. Dispensing stations are arranged in a token
ring; the loading token circulates and only the node holding it may load a
prescription. Prescriptions wait in a request pool before loading, and a loaded
prescription is later dispensed off the tray. A station may crash silently, after
which it simply forwards the token on its next turn. Actions: pass the loading
token to the next station, submit a prescription request to the pool, load a
requested prescription onto the tray (token holder, only while the tray has room),
dispense a prescription off the tray, crash a station silently.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of prescriptions on the dispensing tray never exceeds
the fixed tray capacity Cap.

---- MODULE W4Od6m0p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

Cars == {"c1", "c2"}
Calls == {"h1", "h2"}
none == "none"

VARIABLES version, pool, owner, claims
vars == << version, pool, owner, claims >>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..2
    /\ pool \subseteq Calls
    /\ owner \in [Calls -> Cars \cup {none}]
    /\ claims \subseteq (Cars \X Calls \X (0..2))

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ pool = Calls
    /\ owner = [c \in Calls |-> none]
    /\ claims = {}

Stage(car, call) ==
    /\ call \in pool
    /\ << car, call, version >> \notin claims
    /\ claims' = claims \cup {<< car, call, version >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, pool, owner >>

Commit(car, call) ==
    /\ << car, call, version >> \in claims
    /\ call \in pool
    /\ pool' = pool \ {call}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![call] = car]
    /\ version' = (version + 1) % 3
    /\ claims' = claims \ {<< car, call, version >>}

DropStale(car, call, v) ==
    /\ << car, call, v >> \in claims
    /\ v # version
    /\ claims' = claims \ {<< car, call, v >>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, pool, owner >>

Release(call) ==
    /\ owner[call] # none
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![call] = none]
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {call}
    /\ UNCHANGED << version, claims >>

Next ==
    \/ \E car \in Cars, call \in Calls : Stage(car, call)
    \/ \E car \in Cars, call \in Calls : Commit(car, call)
    \/ \E car \in Cars, call \in Calls, v \in 0..2 : DropStale(car, call, v)
    \/ \E call \in Calls : Release(call)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PoolIffUnowned == \A c \in Calls : (c \in pool) <=> (owner[c] = none)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PoolIffUnowned
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper assigns hall calls to cars using optimistic
locking over a shared assignment version. Each hall call is either in the
unassigned pool or owned by exactly one car. A car stages a claim on a pooled
call, recording the version it observed; staged claims arrive asynchronously and
can be reordered in an unordered set. A claim commits only if the call is still
pooled and the observed version still matches, assigning the call to the car,
removing it from the pool, and bumping the version. A stale claim whose version no
longer matches is dropped. An owned call may be released back to the pool.
Actions: stage a claim (reorderable), commit a matching claim, drop a stale claim,
release an owned call.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A hall call is in the unassigned pool if and only if it has no
owning car, so no call is ever allocated to two cars at once.
